drafts.question_theme: What does the Wheel of Fortune tarot card mean?
drafts.answer: The Wheel of Fortune is card number 10 of the Major Arcana and it is the tarot's card of cycles. In the Rider-Waite image a great wheel turns in the sky with a sphinx holding a sword on top, a serpent sliding down one side and a jackal-headed figure rising on the other, while four winged creatures in the corners sit reading books. The composition makes the argument: everything turns except the part of you that watches and learns. Upright, most readers take it as a turning point, a stalled situation starting to move, timing shifting in your favour. The useful reading is less about luck and more about timing: the cycle has reached its bend, so act while conditions work for you, because wheels do not stop at the top either. Reversed, it usually describes resisting a change already underway, or a repeating pattern, the same job problem with a new employer, the same argument with a new partner. In love it often marks a relationship entering a new phase. In money it points at fluctuation, so build the buffer during the upswing. The card never promises comfort. It promises movement.

drafts.question_theme: What does the Ace of Cups mean for how someone sees you?
drafts.answer: The Ace of Cups is one of the warmest answers you can get in a how-someone-sees-you position. Aces are beginnings and cups are the suit of feeling, so the card is emotion arriving for the first time. In the Rider-Waite image a hand reaches from a cloud holding a golden cup, five streams of water overflow into a lotus-covered sea, and a dove descends toward the cup. Upright, it suggests the person sees you as a beginning rather than a chapter of an old story. Talking to you feels easy, their guard drops around you, and they catch themselves looking forward to the next conversation. In a romantic context it reads as a crush with substance: not just attraction, but something tender and a little undefended. The one caution is newness. An ace is a seed, not a harvest, so the feeling is honest but untested. Reversed, the card describes feeling that cannot get out, either their guard from an old hurt or your warmth flickering in a way they cannot read. The practical advice for the upright card is simple: stop auditing the offer for flaws and answer it.

drafts.question_theme: Are Gemini and Sagittarius a good match?
drafts.answer: Gemini and Sagittarius sit opposite each other on the zodiac wheel, and oppositions are the loudest pairings in astrology. Both are mutable signs, curious, restless and allergic to routine, which is why the pair so often starts as the two people talking until the party closes. The difference is altitude. Gemini, an air sign ruled by Mercury, wants to know a little about everything. Sagittarius, a fire sign ruled by Jupiter, wants one big truth to aim at. When it works, each covers what the other misses: Gemini hands Sagittarius lightness and honest questions, Sagittarius hands Gemini direction and a reason the trivia matters. The clashes are just as predictable. Gemini flits between plans and opinions, which Sagittarius experiences as flaky. Sagittarius delivers blunt truth and calls it integrity, which Gemini experiences as being hit. And both signs dodge the ordinary maintenance of a shared life. The couples that last build novelty into the ordinary, say the jealousy rules out loud early, and translate the honesty, Gemini says the direct version once, Sagittarius says the blunt version once kindly. Astrology is a reflection tool rather than a verdict, but as oppositions go this one starts with more natural ease than most.
